correctness.rationale: For normal P the Brauer kernel is spanned by nontrivial P-orbit sums and lies in J(kG), hence is nilpotent. This identifies the semisimple quotient with that of kC_G(P), yielding the locality criterion. In the local noncentral case, the full group sum and a nonzero socle submodule of the Brauer kernel are independent socle contributions, ruling out self-injectivity. The central case is a symmetric group algebra. Under fixed-point-free outside action, outside P-orbits are cosets and direct multiplication gives the stated square-zero extension.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Danz--Ellers--Murray provide the normal-p-subgroup Brauer-kernel input and Allan proves non-self-injectivity for noncentral subgroup fixed algebras inside p-group algebras, but targeted current searches did not locate the combined locality classification, the exact self-injective/Frobenius/symmetric criterion for arbitrary ambient finite G, or the explicit fixed-point-free square-zero structure.

value.rationale: The result gives exact group-theoretic criteria for locality and, within the local family, self-injectivity/Frobenius/symmetry, plus a concrete square-zero model for Frobenius-kernel type actions. It supplies both a structural mechanism and broad counterexample families for modular centralizer algebras.
